standard_prerequisites.name: The shifted complex of a complex M with respect to a nonzerodivisor f has i-th term f^i M^i and differentials induced by the differentials of M
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 27504-27506, where the cycles of the shifted complex are computed
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the cohomology of the shifted complex into a quotient of f^i times the cycles of M.

standard_prerequisites.name: The kernel of the differential in degree i of the shifted complex equals f^i ker(d^i), because multiplication by f^i is injective on M^i and on M^{i+1} when f is a nonzerodivisor on all terms
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that multiplication by f^i lands in the cycles of the shifted complex and induces a surjection on cohomology.

standard_prerequisites.name: An element of the kernel of the induced map on cohomology satisfies f^i z = d(f^{i-1} y), which after cancelling f^i and f^{i-1} means f z = d(y), that is z is f-torsion in cohomology
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the kernel of the surjection with the f-torsion subgroup of H^i(M), which yields the displayed isomorphism.

core_obligations: Compute the cycles in degree i of the shifted complex: observe that ker(d^i : (eta_f M)^i -> (eta_f M)^{i+1}) equals ker(d^i : f^i M^i -> f^i M^{i+1}), which equals f^i ker(d^i : M^i -> M^{i+1}) (proof lines 27503-27506).
Deduce that multiplication by f^i gives a surjection from H^i(M) onto H^i(eta_f M), by sending the class of a cycle z to the class of f^i z (proof lines 27507-27510).

Compute the kernel of that surjection: if the class of f^i z becomes zero then f^i z = d^{i-1}(f^{i-1} y) for some y, and since f is a nonzerodivisor on the terms involved this cancels to f z = d^{i-1}(y), which says exactly that the class of z is f-torsion (proof lines 27510-27514).
Conclude that the induced map f^i identifies the quotient of H^i(M) by its f-torsion subgroup with H^i(eta_f M), which is the displayed canonical isomorphism (proof lines 27507-27515).
proof_roadmap: Identify the cycles of the shifted complex in degree i with f^i times the cycles of M in degree i, using that f is a nonzerodivisor on the terms of the complex (proof lines 27503-27506).
Read off a surjection on cohomology given by multiplication by f^i (proof lines 27507-27510).
Compute its kernel: an element of the kernel satisfies f z = d(y) after cancelling a power of f, which is precisely the condition that its class is f-torsion (proof lines 27510-27514).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a ring A with a nonzerodivisor f, a complex M of f-torsion free A-modules, and the shifted complex eta_f M whose i-th term is f^i M^i; it asserts that multiplication by f^i induces a canonical isomorphism from the quotient of H^i(M) by its f-torsion subgroup onto H^i(eta_f M) (statement lines 27493-27501). The proof is short but it carries the two computations that make the isomorphism canonical: the cycles of the shifted complex are identified with f^i times the cycles of M using injectivity of multiplication by f on the terms, and the kernel of the resulting surjection is computed by cancelling a factor f^{i-1} from the equation f^i z = d(f^{i-1} y), which is exactly the point at which the nonzerodivisor hypothesis is used (proof lines 27503-27514).
